# Miso Music Protocol

> Developer documentation for the Miso Music Protocol, a small set of Sui Move primitives for identifying musical compositions, recordings, and releases and connecting them to optional rights, metadata, and payment packages.

The core Move package is `miso_music`. A `Composition` is the written work, a `Recording` is a particular master with an immutable composition ID, and a `Release` is an ordered list of recording IDs. Each composition and recording has its own fixed-supply share type. Admin capabilities control extension writes and release consent; owning shares alone does not grant those powers.

Read the music overview first, then Shares, Composition, Recording, Release, and the separate Party protocol. The Miso Packages sidebar groups Protocol, Protocol Extensions, and Framework; both protocol groups include Composition, Recording, Release, and Party. These pages explain the protocol design with inline excerpts from the actual Move contracts; use the supplemental Move source guide only when inspecting the implementation. Add only the extensions needed for the product. A core object link is not proof of real-world authorship or a license, and holding shares pays nothing by itself: payment depends on a funded royalty pool and registered stakes. Pin compatible source revisions and verify published package IDs before constructing transactions against a network.

## Start Here

- [Overview](https://docs.miso.fm/protocol/overview/index.md): The song/master/release model, industry identifier lookups and access, Music's Shared Ledger, the limits of canonical state, and Miso Link's SuiNS bridge.

## Protocol

- [Shares](https://docs.miso.fm/protocol/shares/index.md): Why each work has a distinct share type and fixed supply, the contract's supply constants, how initial allocation differs from minting, and how shares, administration, and royalty participation differ.
- [Composition](https://docs.miso.fm/protocol/composition/index.md): Why the written work has an identity independent of recordings, its unique share type, its minimal Move definition, capability-gated extension access, and optional extensions.
- [Recording](https://docs.miso.fm/protocol/recording/index.md): Why a master has independent identity and shares, an immutable composition relationship, its Move object and publication event definitions, and separate consent for each release.
- [Release](https://docs.miso.fm/protocol/release/index.md): Ordered track lists, identity committed to order and salt, inline object and consent definitions, the contract's consent-target check, release administration, and the separation of presentation and commercial terms.

- [Party](https://docs.miso.fm/protocol/party/index.md): The separate `miso_party` identity protocol for individuals and groups, mutable names, object-bound admin capabilities, consent-based membership, attribution, and unverified identity claims.

## Packages, Protocol Extensions, and Framework

- [Packages Overview](https://docs.miso.fm/packages/index.md): How core identities, data-model extensions, and business-logic framework packages fit together; core share validation, identifier resolution, compatibility, and licensing.
- [Protocol Extensions Overview](https://docs.miso.fm/packages/protocol-extensions/index.md): Optional typed data for music objects and parties, with object-specific inventories, cap-gated writes, and permissionless reads.
- [Composition Extensions](https://docs.miso.fm/packages/protocol-extensions/composition/index.md): Titles, songwriting and publishing credits, and lyrics from music-protocol-extensions.
- [Recording Extensions](https://docs.miso.fm/packages/protocol-extensions/recording/index.md): Version labels, performance credits, advisory status, genres, and languages.
- [Release Extensions](https://docs.miso.fm/packages/protocol-extensions/release/index.md): Titles, cover art, top-line credits, descriptions, genres, and release kind.
- [Party Extensions](https://docs.miso.fm/packages/protocol-extensions/party/index.md): Profiles, roles, genres, tags, media, CTAs, platform links, and pure link-payload packages. The inline profile excerpt retains FSL-1.1-ALv2.
- [Framework](https://docs.miso.fm/packages/framework/index.md): Reusable business-logic packages for licensing, royalties, payments, custody, workflows, streaming, and commerce, plus supporting utilities.
- [Royalty Pools](https://docs.miso.fm/packages/royalty-pool/index.md): Pool creation, stake registration, deposits, settlement, claims, and payout trust boundaries.
- [Recording Licenses](https://docs.miso.fm/packages/recording-license/index.md): Optional standing composition policy, recording-share cut, and revenue sweep into a composition pool.

## Optional

- [Move Source Guide](https://docs.miso.fm/protocol/integrating/index.md): Supplemental implementation material: reproduce the pinned core tests, inspect dependencies and constructor tests, and distinguish source revisions from network deployments.

## Complete Text and Terms

- [Complete Documentation](https://docs.miso.fm/llms-full.txt): All substantive docs pages in one text file, generated from the same Markdown sources as this site.
- [Documentation Licensing](https://docs.miso.fm/licensing/index.md): CC BY 4.0 for original prose and diagrams; Apache 2.0 for independently written examples and site software. Copied or adapted package excerpts retain their source licenses, including FSL-1.1-ALv2 where applicable. Inclusion in the docs does not relicense FSL excerpts; the FSL future Apache grant applies separately to each version after two years.

## Source Repositories

- [Miso Music Protocol](https://github.com/misofm/music-protocol): Core Move package, templates, source modules, and Apache 2.0 license.
- [Party Protocol](https://github.com/misofm/party-protocol): Apache-2.0 identity primitive in `miso_party`, separate from the music core.
- [Party Extensions](https://github.com/misofm/party-protocol-extensions): FSL-1.1-ALv2 profile extensions and typed link-payload packages.
- [Miso Link](https://github.com/misofm/link): SuiNS-based mapping of legacy industry identifiers to on-chain object addresses. A mapping is an assertion by its namespace controller, not an official registry record or rights verification.
